tables.description: Comparison of theoretical and experimental studies based on developing and emerging concepts at the intersection of neuroscience and architecture.
Outcomes extracted from experimental articles, categorized by emerging concepts, human experience, built environment features, and measurement techniques.

limitations: Most experimental studies were conducted in contrived settings (laboratories, VR studios), which are not wholly adequate for thoroughly understanding human experience.
Psychophysiological measurements collected a large amount of raw data, making meaningful inferences difficult for researchers.
Exposure to all types of external stimuli in real-life settings prevented the collection of accurate data about human experience.
Most conceptualization in the field is generated by theoretical studies, and many concepts developed in theoretical frameworks have not yet been verified in experimental works.
The concepts presented in theoretical studies and examined in experimental studies do not match.
Experimental studies face challenges in measuring and associating data, and have thus far touched only a small part of the theoretical output.
A large array of concepts requires further research.
